paper_sections.title: Altered regional activity and connectivity of functional brain networks in congenital unilateral conductive hearing loss
Differences in regional activity and connectivity
Ethics approval and consent to participate

description.value: The study investigated altered resting-state regional spontaneous activity and seed-based functional connectivity in patients with right-sided congenital unilateral microtia and severe hearing loss compared with age- and sex-matched normal-hearing controls, including the effects of global signal regression and associations with clinical variables.

design.value: A cross-sectional case-control resting-state fMRI study compared 24 patients with right-sided congenital unilateral microtia after quality-control exclusions with 25 age- and sex-matched normal-hearing controls. Regional activity was assessed with ALFF, fALFF and ReHo, and seed-based functional connectivity was assessed using clusters showing between-group regional-activity differences. Analyses were performed with and without global signal regression.

description.value: Hearing level was assessed in a closed field at six frequencies (0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8 kHz).
Cognitive abilities were evaluated using the Mini-Mental State Examination.
Cognitive abilities were evaluated using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment test.

description.value: Functional images were obtained axially with a gradient echo type echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence. The scanning parameters were 36 slices, thickness 4 mm, gap 0 mm, 64 × 64 acquisition matrix, flip-angle 90°, and field of view 200 × 200 mm².

pulse_sequence_type.value: gradient echo type echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence

description.value: Anatomical images were acquired with a high-resolution T1-weighted gradient-echo sequence.

All rs-fMRI images were processed using SPM12 and SeeCAT. The first 10 time points were deleted; slice-timing and head-motion correction were implemented; images were normalized to the EPI template, resampled to 3-mm isotropic voxels and smoothed with a 4-mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian kernel. Confounding signals from white matter and cerebrospinal fluid, linear drift and Friston-24 head-motion parameters were removed using linear regression. Time series were band-pass filtered at 0.01–0.1 Hz. Volumes with >0.5 mm framewise displacement and adjacent volumes were replaced using linear interpolated data.

steps.value: The first 10 time points of the functional imaging were deleted.
Slice-timing and head-motion correction were implemented.
The corrected images were normalized to the EPI template.
Smoothed with a 4-mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian kernel.
White matter, cerebrospinal fluid, linear drift and Friston-24 head-motion parameters were removed using a linear regression model.
Volumes with a >0.5 mm framewise displacement, as well as adjacent volumes, were replaced using linear interpolated data.
Global signal regression was performed in one preprocessing stream and omitted in another.

model_settings.value: ALFF, fALFF, ReHo and SBFC were compared in the two groups with regression of age, gender and educational level. Gaussian random field corrections were used for multiple comparisons (p < 0.001 at the voxel level and p < 0.05 at the cluster level).
The relationship between brain regions showing group differences and clinical features was investigated. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05 with the Bonferroni correction.
